keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Griqualand West; the Cape shape of 1871 absorbs it, see af-07-a). Infobox 'Established: 1800', 'British rule imposed: 1871', 'Dissolved: 1880' and 'Area (estimate): 40,000 km2'; the page draws no boundary, only 'near the junction of the Vaal and Orange rivers'; drawn as the gazetteer's Griqualand West region (confidence 1 for the pre-1871 outline). [Repair 2026-10-19: the shape is held to 1880 as this dossier's own; British sovereignty from 27 October 1871 is entered as a rename, not a loss. Pre-1871 outline: the Griqua people page was opened for the thin item and gives no boundaries ('near the Orange River just west and south of what would eventually become' the Boer republics; Waterboer 'founded Griqualand West'; Nicholas Waterboer 'ruled the farthest west of Kimberley'), no founding year for the Griqua state and no Keate Award, so the pre-1871 outline stays at confidence 1.]

ledger.note: c. 1800: the Griqua polity of Griqualand West is established. Infobox 'Established: 1800'; the Griqua capital was Klaarwater (Griquatown) and 'Andries Waterboer took over control and founded the powerful Waterboer dynasty'.

ledger.note: 30 July 1870: diggers proclaim the Klipdrift Republic on the diamond fields. 'Stafford Parker declared the Klipdrift Republic on 30 July 1870.'

27 October 1871: the Griqua polity becomes British territory under the same borders. 'on 27 October 1871 the district, together with some adjacent territory ... was proclaimed (under the name of Griqualand West Colony) British territory' after the Keate Award; infobox 'British rule imposed: 1871', 'Status: British Colony (1871-1880)'; 'In 1873 it was proclaimed as a British colony, with its capital at Kimberley'. The land and the extent are unchanged, so this is a change of sovereignty inside one state, not a loss; the colour continues (rule 2). The page does not say that the Cape Colony held the territory before the union of 18 October 1880. [Repair 2026-10-19: was a loss of the whole of Griqualand West to british-colonial-empire at confidence 3 although the keyframe kept drawing it, and the Cape dossier (af-07-b) gained it from 'Griqualand West' in 1871-10 and drew it as its own, so the land was drawn by two or three states for nine years. Routing for af-07-b: the Cape's 1871-10 gain from 'Griqualand West' should go (the Cape gains it by the merge of 18 October 1880).]
1873: Griqualand West becomes a Crown colony: 'In 1873 it was proclaimed as a British colony, with its capital at' Kimberley.

notes: Cliopatria has no Griqualand West (the af-07-a Cape dossier draws it as part of the Cape from 1871). One page opened. Not on the page: the 1867 diamond discovery, the 17 October 1871 Keate Award date, the 1876 compensation figure (only 'in full satisfaction of all claims', July 1876), Hay, the 1878 rising. The Free State claim is not typed as a contest because no campaign is described. The Klipdrift Republic (30 July 1870) is a counterpart needing a dossier (a short-lived digger republic). The pre-1871 Griqua polity (Adam Kok I, Waterboer, Klaarwater) has only the infobox year 1800 for its start; the Griquatown point is the researcher's own knowledge. Region name Griqualand West is a gazetteer name still to be added. REPAIR 2026-10-19 (after review): the 27 October 1871 event is now a 'rename' (Griqua state to British territory) and the dossier keeps drawing Griqualand West to 18 October 1880, when it merges into the Cape. The Cape dossier (british-cape-colony, af-07-b) still has a gain from 'Griqualand West' in 1871-10 that must go; the page (reopened) says nothing of Cape sovereignty before 1880. The other option the reviewer offered (ending this dossier in 1871 and giving the colony to the Cape) was not taken because the infobox gives 'Status: British Colony (1871-1880)' with its own capital, Kimberley, from 1873.
